thread:
marta: FYI seeing a spike in 502/504s from model-serving across the gpu-pool since ~08:14 UTC. started tracing and it looks DNS-related — lots of DNS timeouts hitting node-local-dns pods on those nodes.

jason: ugh, DNS again. any pattern by AZ/region?

marta: only in us-west-2a and -2b so far. affected nodes are all gpu-rtx-80gb with RDMA enabled.

priya: what do the node-local logs show? can you paste the i/o timeout lines?

marta: here are the important snippets from node-local-dns on gpu-114:
```
2026-02-28T08:15:02Z coredns[1]: read udp 10.244.5.3:53->10.96.0.10:38412: i/o timeout
2026-02-28T08:15:02Z node-dns[1]: upstream query timed out after 2s for redis-service.svc.cluster.local
```

kevin: that read udp i/o timeout + RDMA on those hosts screams MTU/fragmentation on the overlay. UDP DNS can get dropped if fragments are lost.

jason: did we see any netdrops/ifdown or kernel ring errors?

marta: ran tcpdump on node and saw a bunch of "IP fragmented" and also some RSTs on TCP 53 when fallback happened. snippet: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 53` showed a lot of truncated EDNS responses.

net-bot: (automated) noticed MTU mismatch between host eth0 (9000) and vxlan0 (1450) on gpu nodes last deploy.

priya: oh interesting — we pushed jumbo frames on hosts but the overlay uses default vxlan MTU. that can break fragmentation when GSO/GRO/GSOv4 interact with vxlan.

kevin: quick checks: 1) disable GSO on vxlan on one node (`ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off`) 2) lower host MTU to 1500 temporarily 3) tcpdump + dig to validate.

marta: did a quick dig against cluster DNS from pod: `dig @10.244.5.3 redis-service.svc.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=1` -> frequently times out; direct to coredns svc IP succeeded but with 200-300ms latency.

jason: so node-local is dropping/losing UDP responses, then apps fall back to TCP which adds latency and causes grpc timeouts. fits the 5xx symptoms.

priya: can we try a narrow mitigation: increase node-local-dns upstream timeout to 5s and scale node-local-dns → 2 replicas per node? also add retry in the client for DNS lookup?

kevin: mitigation plan: 1) roll a patch to set vxlan MTU to 1400 across gpu nodes (net team will do) 2) disable GSO on vxlan during the rolling patch 3) bump coredns/node-local timeout and scale to absorb transient drops 4) add DNS latency alerting (p95,p99) and tcpdump sampler.

marta: I'm going to open a short incident to track. Ops: enable temporary autopilot - reduce model-server concurrency by 25% to avoid cascading errors.

ops-bot: (action) incident-1234 opened: "node-local DNS timeouts on gpu-pool — likely MTU/overlay fragmentation" assigned to @kevin and @priya.

net-bot: ETA for MTU patch: 30m for canary 2 nodes, then 2h for full roll. will post results.

jason: thanks. one small follow up — check conntrack table size and iptables REDIRECT rules for node-local dns (sometimes REDIRECT stalls with high conntrack churn).

priya: good call. I see conntrack high-water on a couple nodes. will increase conntrack and add a short lived cleanup job during the roll.

kevin: once MTU fix is in, let's validate with: 1) dig with +dnssec +edns=0 to avoid large EDNS responses 2) tcpdump confirming fewer fragments 3) app traces show reduced DNS lookup latency and 5xx fall.

marta: noted. I'll update incident and paste before/after histograms. thanks team :thumbsup:
